en.hubeali: H 14682 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al-Hassan Bin Mahboub, who said, ‘we have been informed by Al-Nazar bin Qarwaash Al-Jammaal who said:

I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the camels who have scabies whether I should keep my camel away from these fearing it might get infected by the scabies, and the animals might have got it until it drank the water’.

So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said that: ‘A Bedouin came up to the Rasool Allah<sup>s</sup><sup>aww</sup>. He said, ‘O Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup>, I come across injured sheep, cows, and the camels sold at a cheap price, but they have scabies. I dislike buying these fearing that they may infect my camels and my sheep with that scabies’.
So the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Bedouin! So who infected the first (infected) one?’

Then the Rasool Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is neither infection, nor bad omen, nor ghost, nor bad luck, nor ‘Safra’, nor breastfeeding after weaning, nor being a Bedouin after Migration (Hijra), nor Fasting of silence for a day to the night, nor divorce before the marriage, nor emancipation before slavery, nor being an orphan after achieving adulthood’.
